entities.summary:
Richard of Saint Victor was a Medieval Scottish philosopher and theologian who played a pivotal role in shaping the theological landscape of his time. As a canon regular and prior of the famous Augustinian Abbey of Saint Victor in Paris, he synthesized the teachings of Aristotle, Plato, and the Church Fathers to create a distinctive mystical theology. His work, particularly his treatise 'De Natura Rerum,' had a profound impact on the development of Scholasticism and the intellectual currents of the High Middle Ages. The influence of Richard of Saint Victor can be seen in the thought of prominent figures such as Thomas Aquinas and Peter Abelard, and his emphasis on the importance of contemplation and the inner life resonated with the spiritual aspirations of medieval Christians. The legacy of Richard of Saint Victor continues to be felt in modern theological debates, with his ideas on the nature of God, the universe, and human existence remaining relevant to contemporary discussions of spirituality and the search for meaning.

Born unknown, Richard of Saint Victor died on March 10, 1173, at the age of approximately 61, and was buried in the Abbey of Saint Victor in Paris.

Richard of Saint Victor was a key figure in the intellectual and spiritual currents of the High Middle Ages, and his work continues to be studied and admired by scholars and theologians today.
